status.en: 180 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 24% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Plateau State.
status.nb: 180 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 24 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Plateau State.

summary.en: Bandits and Islamist fighters are intensifying attacks across northern Nigeria, killing an immigration officer in Niger, a traditional ruler in Plateau, and a Christian Red Cross volunteer in the northwest, while abducting farmers, a supervisory councillor, and other civilians in Niger, Kaduna and Zamfara. Boko Haram and ISWAP militants continue to strike military posts in Borno, causing soldiers to be feared killed. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter og islamistiske krigere intensiverer angrep over hele Nord-Nigeria, og dreper en immigrasjons­offiser i Niger, en tradisjons­hersker i Plateau og en kristen Røde Kors-frivillig i nord-vest, mens de bortfører bønder, en tilsynsrådgiver og andre sivile i Niger, Kaduna og Zamfara. Boko Haram og ISWAP-militanter fortsetter å angripe militærposter i Borno, noe som gjør at soldater fryktes drept. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
